I can’t open or edit attachments here — there’s no spreadsheet tool available in this session and you didn’t paste any rows — so I cannot change your workbook. Below is a concise, safe, concrete next step you can run in your spreadsheet (Excel or Google Sheets) to clean duplicates and fix broken date formats while keeping formulas intact.

Immediate precaution
- Make a backup copy of the workbook (File > Save a copy) before doing anything.

Quick inspection (do this first)
1. Identify which columns contain formulas versus raw data:
   - Excel: Formulas > Show Formulas (or Ctrl+`) to see where formulas are.
   - Google Sheets: View > Show formulas.
   - Note any formulas that depend on specific row positions (absolute references, SUM ranges, etc.). If formulas depend on row order or specific row counts, avoid deleting rows in-place — use the “clean copy” method below.

Fix broken date formats (use a helper column; don’t overwrite original until verified)
- Create a helper column next to the date column (e.g., Date_Clean).
- Excel helper (coerce many text dates to real dates):
  =IF(A2="", "", IFERROR(VALUE(A2), IFERROR(DATEVALUE(A2), "")))
- Google Sheets helper:
  =IF(A2="", "", IFERROR(VALUE(A2), IFERROR(DATEVALUE(A2), "")))
- If date parts are consistently in a nonstandard format (e.g., dd.mm.yyyy), first replace separators:
  Excel: =IF(A2="", "", IFERROR(VALUE(SUBSTITUTE(A2,".","/")), ""))
- After the helper column shows correct dates, format it as Date. Verify a sample of rows.
- Once verified, copy the helper column → Paste special > Values over the original date column (only after confirming no formulas will break).

Remove duplicates (two safe approaches)

A. In-place (only if formulas don’t rely on absolute row positions)
- Select the full data range (include headers).
- Excel: Data > Remove Duplicates → select the key columns that define a unique customer (Customer ID, Email — do NOT include columns that contain only formulas you want to retain).
- Google Sheets: Data > Data cleanup > Remove duplicates → select the key columns.
- Verify results against the backup.

B. Create a clean copy (safer, recommended when formulas may break)
- Create a new sheet named Cleaned.
- Copy headers to Cleaned.
- Use a unique-values extraction on core data columns (values only), then reapply formulas as needed:
  - Google Sheets: =UNIQUE( {range_of_key_and_value_columns} )
  - Excel: Data > Remove Duplicates on a copied values-only range, or use Power Query: Data > From Table/Range → Remove Duplicates → Close & Load.
- Reconnect or re-copy formulas: keep original workbook unchanged while you verify the cleaned dataset. Only replace originals after confirming everything.

Final verification
- Check totals and summary formulas (if any) to ensure they still reference the intended ranges.
- If formulas used whole-column or structured references, confirm they still cover the cleaned rows or update their ranges.

If you want, paste a small, de-identified sample (10–20 rows including header row) here (no sensitive PII) or tell me whether you use Excel or Google Sheets and whether formulas are row-by-row or in a summary area. I can give a tailored step-by-step sequence or exact helper formulas to run.
